The **hjemkommune** (home municipality) refers to the local municipal authority responsible for a patient's primary social and healthcare support within the Danish system. In the context of the ADHD Database evaluations, the home municipality has been established as the central actor in the revised [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]], a quality metric designed to evaluate and enforce cross-sectoral collaboration for ADHD patients [^src1].

Originally, Indicator 4 measured the completion of coordinating network meetings during ADHD treatment courses. However, chronic failures to meet this target across regions and departments prompted the steering group to structurally evaluate and strategically revise the indicator [^src1]. The revised version abandons the network meeting requirement in favor of a more operational and cross-sectorally realistic metric focused on the diagnostic assessment phase [^src1]. 

Under the new guidelines, the fulfillment of [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] is measured specifically by the proportion of assessment processes where the patient's home municipality is contacted within 120 days after the start of the assessment [^src1]. This shift underscores the municipality's critical role in ensuring realistic cooperation and reflects a broader political and clinical recognition that effective ADHD intervention requires early, structured coordination between specialized psychiatry and the primary sector [^src1].
